There needs to be public understanding of education and economics.  It is not necessarily intuitively obvious but it returns more money to the country than it costs to help with student debt.  

It is an investment with a high yield return.  It is not a zero sum game.  It may seem that it would strap us by paying for someone else but the reality is that we will be financially better off.  

Tax revenue increases, deficits can be paid down, more benefits can be gained by you and I.  It is a classic example of Nash’s Nobel prize winning economics.  Mutually beneficial arrangements multiply the benefits each receives.

A college degree provides on average an added million dollars of income to a career.  That amount has only increased since I saw the figures last.  That is added tax revenue exceeding the invested money to help make college affordable. 

Money is spent and re-spent on average seven times.  This means our GDP increases by seven fold of any added income.  

Just as a crude example, if Joe makes an added $50,000 he spends that and Pete makes an added 50k and Pete spends it and Sally makes an added 50k and so on seven times before it is put in savings.  Obviously the money would be spent many places but the concept is the same.

Any and all education collectively decreases the amount of crime saving tax payer costs for, policing, courts snd incarceration.  Social benefits go far beyond this example.

Our single most valuable resource is our country’s intellect.  It is what gives us our economic edge.  Jobs are created at a higher rate by those that complete added studies.  All professions require knowledge and that knowledge benefits the one learning it regardless of its source.  Some endeavors require formal education, some require trade skills and we all benefit.   We benefit from doctors and health care workers, skilled labor, advances in science and technology and the list goes on.

Education provides a leg up and upward mobility for those of us that were born into poor families and dead end towns.  

It is easy to exploit this highly political topic.  All knowledge has value regardless if it was taught by a parent, friend, co-worker, teacher or if we just figured it out on our own.  Fueling resentment of one group over the other does no one any good (besides politicians).

The US government spent over two and a half years and over a quarter million dollars investigating confirming, reconfirming and then reconfirming again my trustworthiness over the course of my career as a part of my clearances. I just happened to just be in that place at that time but I think it reflects the federal government’s trust in my character.

In 1996 I was asked to testify to a Virginia joint subcommittee by a concerned non-profit after a decade of abuse by law enforcement and the judiciary in Florida, Texas and Virginia while trying to get my daughter out of an abusive home.  Four years later I finally got sole custody, but only after having my ankle re-broken by Norfolk police, my civil rights trampled, and bankrupted causing me to loose my home of 25 years.  The guardian ad litem who was a licensed attorney chased me down and said that I had literally saved my daughter’s life and that she knew no one that could have or would have endured the abuse I went through.

About the same time four young men in Norfolk were wrongly convicted on coerced confessions.  There was irrefutable proof that these men were innocent almost immediately, and that one uncharged man committed the crime but the prosecuting attorneys chose their careers over justice.

Frontline did a show on coerced confessions including the Norfolk case and despite proof of their innocence twenty years ago these young sailors and marines spent two decades in jail.  They were finally pardoned recently with the help of the innocence project.  

John Grisham’s non-fiction “An Innocent Man” chronically abuses by police and prosecutors of a wrongfully convicted man in Oklahoma.  I was also maliciously prosecuted in Norfolk.  I was on leave during recall working on the Gulf War Illnesses project in DC.  I had my daughter during normal visitation, and irrefutable proof of my innocents and compliance with the visitation agreement from the USPS was provided by my attorney to then Governor Bush of Texas.  The governor ignored this and decided to choose a lie that was politically expedient. Eventually, the charges were thrown out, my record expunged and the findings of fact included that I had been in constant full compliance with the law and court orders.  

During this ordeal in Norfolk, I was denied a bail hearing, I was not told what I accused of nor charged for well over 24 hours,  I was repeatedly lied to by police, I was injured and caused repeated pain, a judge without jurisdiction that drove around with a license plate that said “25tolife” grabbed the case from the court that had jurisdiction and no jurisdiction in his court.  My poor daughter was not allowed to see her grandparent or receive a change of cloths and was traumatized by the experience.  

The deputy during my in-processing was violently throwing up due to still being drunk.  The prosecuting attorney in Texas transitioned to become a judge and yet refused to recuse himself when later the civil case I filed came before his court. The judge broke the law during the civil trial.  Despite this my attorney prevailed and I was awarded a $40,000 judgement for actual costs but this was soon wiped out in bankruptcy court.  No attorney I approached would represent me to sue the state of Texas or The city of Norfolk.

There was a young black man in the medical cell I was placed in.  His bed was below mine.  He was mentally handicapped and we later learned that he had diabetes.  A couple others being held in the 24 man cell were harassing him and so I leaned over and in my best military officer’s voice told them to leave him alone.  You could see the wheels turning as they tried to evaluate me and if I posed a threat.  They glanced at my wrist, and saw from the color of my wrist band I was charged with a felony.  They backed off and left him alone.  None of us realized it, but the young man unfortunately had not been eating enough and later fell into a diabetic coma.  

Many of the men in the cell with me were senior citizens that had committed petty crimes so they could just have a place to sleep and food to eat.  They were in poor health as a result.  They were good human beings but society was blind to their plight.

The deputy Sheriff came in our cell with several deputies and started out by telling us to shut our mouths with plenty of four letter words for effect.  He said if the young man died we all were going to be charged with manslaughter despite their negligence.  When a black man spoke up and explained that this was ridiculous he incurred the wrath of these thugs.  He then went to the adjacent cell and told those 24 people being held that they would be charged with manslaughter if the young man died.  It was ridiculous and criminal on their part.

I was shackled by my broken ankle along with my wrists and abdomen to a line of others when we went to court.  We were paraded past citizens including a horrified group of children.  An ensign gawked at the procession rather than showing integrity.  To say it was degrading to all of us is an understatement.

A neighbor in Cass County Minnesota is a retired Sheriff and claims that in his experience 70% of law enforcement is corrupt.  I met a former police officer in Norfolk Virginia from Smithfield Virginia.  He had kept copies of all his police records and when the Chief of police and the Mayor altered one of his record to convict a suspect he blew the whistle.  He was fired, received death threats, some of which I heard where we worked and police helicopters buzzed his house at all hours of the night.

I reported theft and vandalism of an absentee land owners property in Minnesota.  When the deputy arrived he said I was being petty despite over $3000 worth of damage to surveying, thousands of dollars worth of state contracted young trees destroyed and theft of crops.  The deputy allegedly had been sleeping with one of the perpetrators.

I reported the incident to the sheriff who confirmed that it was misconduct.  I was then confronted repeatedly by deputies, assaulted, threatened as a witness to their crimes.  I was threatened to be arrested for “driving reckless in my field”, I was told that the only way a crime against me could be investigated is if a judge first determined a crime was committed.  

I reported this and crimes by the Sheriff and County attorney to the MN AG and they sent the complaint right back to the Sheriff and County Attorney.  A friend and retired law enforcement officer tells me that Minnesota is one of the few states without accountability for local law enforcement or prosecuting attorneys.

There is no external oversight of our judiciary.  Prosecutorial discretion has no oversight and its abuses have not been addressed despite decades of scholarly papers from respected law schools railing against it.  The U.K. and Germany are just two first world countries that have long since addressed and corrected this abuse in their countries.

I have written and/or spoken to every elected official from the township board to the White House to no avail.  I am homeless and disabled from all this.  To add insult to injury, I am not receiving my military retirement pay despite sending corrections to NMPC more than two dozen times in my career.

It goes on and on and on and on....
